newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine o/night, secondary T-bill rates firmer.
newsitem.headline: Philippine o/night, secondary T-bill rates firmer.

text.p: Tight liquidity pushed Philippine overnight money higher on Monday to 11.78125 percent as banks have either placed their funds in dollars or termed reverse repos, traders said.
The rate was 11.09375 percent on Friday.
One trader said that reverse repos, left untouched by the Central Bank for two weeks, offer attractive rates for resale to their clients.
The Central Bank has been offering one-month reverse repos at 11.25 percent, two-months at 11.375 percent, and three-months at 11.5 percent.
Another trader said many banks have been investing in dollars and covering their short-term peso requirements through the interbank market.
The dollars have been rising against the peso. The peso slipped to 25.246 in early Monday trade from 25.243 at Friday's close.
A total of 18.102 billion pesos was traded in the interbank market, with done rates hitting a high of 13.0 percent.
The liquidity tightness had also influenced the secondary rates of government securities.
Prior to the weekly Treasury bill auction, three-month bills were trading at 11.4 to 11.6 percent, significantly higher than last week's 11.3 percent auction rate.
Six-month bill rates were at 11.8 percent, and one-year bills at 12.75 percent.
Traders expected the auction rates to inch up by 10 to 20 basis points across all maturities.
